A frame from a black-and-white film noir of the 1940s, re-created as a hand-painted background for a narrative adventure game. Strictly monochrome: only pure black, white and neutral greys; no colour at all, no sepia, no blue or warm tint. Very high contrast chiaroscuro lighting: more than half of the picture is deep, solid black shadow, with hard, sharp-edged shadow shapes and only a few bright light sources. Strong backlight: a bank of luminous grey fog over the sea is lit from behind, so the masts, the boats, the jetty posts, the lantern post and the edge of the cottage stand as crisp black silhouettes against the glowing fog. Rainy night: the cobbled quay is soaking wet and glossy black, with long, sharp vertical reflections of every light. Atmospheric depth: distant shapes fade into grey fog in clear, separate layers. Painted in a clean, simplified, graphic way: big simple shapes, crisp edges, smooth tonal gradations only in the fog and in the glow of the lights, little texture, no fussy detail. Low cinematic camera at the eye height of a small figure standing on the quay, looking along the quay. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a pencil drawing, not a comic with black outlines, no colour, no film grain, no scratches, no vignette, no frame.

Composition for a fixed side-view adventure game screen in a wide cinema format: the picture will be cropped to a wide band, the top 17% and the bottom 20% are cut off, so keep everything important between 17% and 80% of the picture height. Horizon at about 46% of the picture height. The quay runs as one level band across the whole width of the picture: its back edge at the water runs straight at about 57% of the picture height, and its wet, flat cobbled surface fills the picture from there down to the bottom edge, free and walkable from left to right. On the left (the left fifth of the width) stands the stone harbour-master's cottage, seen a little from the side, with its side wall facing the middle of the picture; in this wall one tall window fitted with closed venetian blinds: the light from inside shines between the horizontal slats as bright parallel lines. The top of its chimney at about 20% of the picture height. The quay to the right of the cottage, from 5% to 48% of the width, stays plain dark wet cobbles without any objects (the striped light falling from the window onto the quay is added later by the game). The lantern post stands at the back edge of the quay at about 56% of the width, its lantern at about 27% of the picture height. The short wooden jetty with the two moored boats leads out into the water between 62% and 80% of the width, half lost in the fog. On the right the rocky headland with the lighthouse at about 87% of the width, the top of the lighthouse at about 21% of the picture height. The two barrels, the stack of crates and the coil of rope stand together at the right edge of the quay, from 84% of the width to the right edge. A small figure about 25% of the picture height tall will later walk along the quay from the left and stop at about 42% of the width, its feet at about 76% of the picture height; the scale of the cottage, the lantern post and the barrels must fit such a figure.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Important for the game version: some things move in the game and are added later as separate animated layers, so paint them exactly as described here, even where the description above says otherwise. Everything is in black and white: the band of light at the horizon is a pale silver-grey glow, the red band of the lighthouse a dark grey band, the stars only a few faint white points in a gap between the clouds. No falling rain and no rain streaks anywhere (the rain is animated), but every surface is wet. The lighthouse lamp only as a small bright spot without any beam (the rotating beam is animated). The lantern glass bright with only a small soft glow around it, no light rays, and its bright reflection on the wet cobbles below it. No smoke above the chimney, no birds. The window blinds bright as described, but no striped light on the ground.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, painted by hand. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the painting and the lighting change. The first reference is a plain grey 3D render: take only the layout and the poses from it, never its smooth plastic shading or its soft, even light. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its colours, its drawing style, its outlines or its three-view layout. The third reference image shows the black-and-white noir painting technique and the tonal range of the game: paint the figures with exactly this technique, but do not copy any of its content.

Painting technique: the same black-and-white film-noir painting as the background of the game (third reference): strictly monochrome, only black, white and neutral greys, with one single exception: the knitted scarf is a strong, saturated deep red, the only colour in the whole picture. Hard theatrical lighting, identical on all ten figures: a hard key light from the upper right and slightly in front (a street lantern ahead of the character) brightly lights the face, the chest, the parcel and the front leg; the back of each figure falls into deep, almost black shadow with a crisp, sharp-edged boundary; a thin bright white rim light runs along the top of the cap, the back of the head and the back. Clean, simplified painted shapes with crisp edges, few big tonal areas instead of fine texture: the fur in flat dark grey and light grey shapes, the broad black-and-white stripes of the face clearly readable, a small bright catchlight in the eye, the cap and the vest dark grey, the shirt light grey, satchel and parcel mid grey, the red scarf modelled only by light and shadow. No outlines, no fur texture, no individual hairs, no soft airbrush, no glossy plastic highlights, no colour except the red scarf. It must look like a painted character of a noir adventure game: not a 3D render, not a photograph, not a plush toy, not a cartoon with outlines.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background, with clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.
